title: Point registryUrl at an attacker mirror to poison the CI re-evaluation

prerequisites: Control of a registry mirror serving forged publish times and provenance
attacker.goal: Make the independent CI re-evaluation read from the attacker's registry so a poisoned package clears release-age and provenance checks.

startingState: A PR edits safeinstall.config.json's registryUrl to https://registry.attacker.example and installs from it. The decision-record verifier re-checks the committed head.
vulnerableVersion: n/a — defended by the D3 verifier-side registry trust root
expectedVerdict: finding: registry-not-default (decisions verify/authorize fails unless the URL is allowlisted verifier-side)
regressionTest: tests/decision-verify.test.ts > treats a non-default registryUrl as a hard finding unless allowlisted (D3)
provenance: RFC-001 §13 K3; closed this cycle by decision D3
